sources.title: Quantum 70 Installation Manual
sources.publisher: HKC Ltd.; original manufacturer manual hosted by GARD Security
sources.scope: Quantum70 V4.0+; UK variant, with documented conditional devices. Reused pages with conflicting model data are called out.

sources.title: Quantum 70 User Manual
sources.publisher: HKC Security; official GB support download
sources.scope: Earlier Quantum70 user procedures. The V4 installer p57 independently corroborates User/Manager menu order; exact V4 user prompt timing still requires hardware verification.

baseline: Quantum70 V4.0+ · installation manual 310118_1; UK options. Earlier official 160811_1 user guide is separately scoped.
supported: Immediate local engineer digits where unambiguous
Zone type/name/options and persistent fictional settings
RF Echo and SABB YES on/off tests
Engineer walk test and local event logs
Authorised * zone [* zone] YES inhibit flow; unset restores
Menu search and SHOW HINTS through shared engine
limitations: Quantum70 only; this profile does not represent SecureWave1070/10270 or later SecureHub.
User guide edition2011 is separated from the V4 installation baseline.
All credentials are already authorised; no factory codes or live transports.
Guided lessons are selected subsets. Full exploration, exact inhibit flow and SHOW HINTS are in the complete emulator.
User-menu entries are unnumbered; engineer quick digits act per level.
Text helpers and unresolved numeric ranges are labelled. Bell automatic timing, radio enrollment and copied manual contradictions remain visible gaps.

gaps.title: User guide predates V4
gaps.reason: The official guide is 2011; installer V4 p57 confirms the User/Manager order, but not every timing/detail of the older arming/inhibit procedure.
gaps.question: Can you record a Quantum70 V4 user entering *5 YES after authorisation, then unsetting, including every display?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Arming options 1 / 10 / 11
gaps.reason: Printed numbers collide under immediate-digit navigation. This menu is scroll-only until the actual input method is verified.
gaps.question: From 81, how do you select Arm Squawk (10) and Infinite Exit (11) without selecting Final Door (1)?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Point Hardware / Block Assign
gaps.reason: Overview p8 and body p56 disagree about local Point Menu numbering. No numeric shortcut is guessed.
gaps.question: On V4, what are Point Menu items 5 and 6, and which actually appear?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: IP Monitoring copied model data
gaps.reason: Detailed p87 uses SecureComm98 and eight blocks, unlike Quantum70 p9 and p3. The top location 974 is documented; details remain reference-only.
gaps.question: Can the Quantum70 V4 IP Monitoring submenu and its block list be recorded?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Camera Image Size source conflict
gaps.reason: p17 says NO toggles and gives an inconsistent VGA resolution; p52 says YES and 640×480. The dedicated menu page is used, with this limitation visible.
gaps.question: Does your Quantum70 V4 use YES or NO to toggle Image Size?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: RF copied model ranges
gaps.reason: RF Echo/SABB pages mention blocks0–8; PIRCAM pages mention RF Points/P50. Those capacities are not extended to Quantum70.
gaps.question: Which block values and RF option labels are actually present on your Quantum70?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: CO test code
gaps.reason: RF device diagrams repeat code2 for CO; SABB already occupies code2. The CO test is kept as an unnumbered reference.
gaps.question: What local number, if any, is displayed beside Test RF CO?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: GSM fault-delay units
gaps.reason: Overview displays minutes; prose describes seconds. A number editor would risk teaching the wrong unit.
gaps.question: What unit and limits appear on the V4 GSM Signal Monitor Fault Delay field?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Automatic Bell Test sequence
gaps.reason: The sequence is documented, but exact durations and phase-confirmation keys are not. No invented physical YES stepping is taught.
gaps.question: Can you record a complete Bell Test, including the outside prompt, timing and any required key presses?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Physical text/number editing
gaps.reason: Text uses a labelled FINDR helper. Many field lengths and numeric bounds are not given; editors expose this limit.
gaps.question: Can we verify field lengths, NO/YES behavior, and date/time/IP editing on a Quantum70 V4 keypad?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Date/time helper sequence
gaps.reason: The source states the date and time formats but does not give every transition key. The two-field helper advances with YES and is labelled as a FINDR simplification.
gaps.question: What exact keys move from the date to time and confirm the final date/time on Quantum70 V4?
gaps.neededEvidence: Quantum70 V4 keypad recording or manufacturer erratum with exact key presses and firmware version.

gaps.title: Conditional event-timer wizard
gaps.reason: The timer types and dependent fields are mapped; the full conditional scheduling state machine is reference-only.
gaps.question: Can each timer type be recorded from type selection through its final day/block/user field?

gaps.title: Full Fast Format type list
gaps.reason: The manual states over50 channel types but does not publish the complete programming enumeration here. Only documented report examples populate fixture records.

gaps.reason: RF enrollment, battery performance, firmware, audio recording, proximity tags, radio/network scans and transmitted reports require hardware. The references do not invent successful outcomes.

notes: RF test siren/strobe are visual fixture states only.
Automatic Bell Test is mapped but its phase progression is not invented.
The guide contains inconsistent copied-model diagrams; those are retained as explicit evidence gaps.
Source files and hashes were inspected; no installer portal or access control was bypassed.
